proof_attempt_summary: D0 supplied the full-class all-horizon square-root order: sqrt(T)/25600 <= R_T^shuffle <= 140 sqrt(T), using an explicit four-moment assigned-vector policy and an all-policy deterministic-table converse. Raw math review passes with no findings and the Pinsker leaf is source-attested, but the scored paper ceiling7 is below field7.4 and no bounded same-scope lift is offered. tldr: Two causal metrics compete for one adaptive treatment probability. The proposed theorem certifies the exact square-root minimax order of the maximum of their expected cumulative reciprocal second-moment costs under shuffled enrollment from an arbitrary bounded fixed table. Four clipped prefix IPW moments yield an explicit constant-time allocation update, and a deterministic fixed-count converse combines early indistinguishability with a proved allowance for negative late-round gains. The guarantee holds for every integer horizon and the original assigned-vector feedback. The sharp leading value and its attaining design remain the substantive open question. The criterion is a conservative Neyman precision proxy; the two coordinate-specific HT variance offsets remain separate.
gap: Published scalar allocation, iid min-max learning, and full-row random-order optimization do not jointly cover a shared two-metric design with assigned-arm observations and a fixed-table terminal oracle. The controlling metric can change under a perturbation too small to learn early.
fill: The matched full-class certificate is \(\sqrt T/25600\le R_T^{\mathrm{shuffle}}\le140\sqrt T\). The prefix policy and converse retain the finite table and the maximum after expectation; the leading-value question evaluates the remaining design uncertainty.
